_README: Hand-written answers for source routines whose name cannot resolve to a
port symbol on its own. tools/port_coverage.py merges this with what it
Every entry must justify itself and a source-tool test enforces it:
the key has to be a routine in a linked .ASM file, the status has to be
one the tool knows, an 'inlined' or 'renamed' entry has to name a port
identifier that really is defined, a 'dead' entry has to have zero
references in the source, and no entry may claim a routine the automatic
pass already resolves -- otherwise the ledger could mask a regression by
asserting something is fine after it stopped being true.
This file is where an unanswered question becomes an answered one. It is
not where an unanswered question goes to be forgotten.

get_opp_plyrmode.note: process_ptrs[CLOSEST_NUM]->PLYRMODE. The port holds the opponent as a pointer rather than a roster index, so every one of the 115 call sites reads o->player_mode directly; there is nothing left for a function to do.

get_process_ptr.note: process_ptrs[n]. The port passes wm_arcade_actor_t pointers around instead of indexing a global process table.

wres_get_but_val_cur.note: The per-wrestler accessors are read_switches' own loop body. wm_read_switches_one computes all six cached readings plus both relative ones in one pass, exactly as read_switches does.

wres_get_stick_rel_cur.note: The facing-relative reading. wm_read_switches_one derives it via wm_stick_flip; note the standalone routine tests the sprite's FLIPH bit where read_switches tests FACING_DIR's PLAYER_RIGHT_BIT.

wres_get_stick_rel_new.note: Same derivation, gated on there being a stick transition this tick.

civani.note: Writes OIMG/OSIZE/OSAG/OCTRL on a display object to swap its image. There is no object system in this port; every animation change ends at a frame-name seam instead.

civanic.note: civani with the object's existing OCTRL preserved. Same reason.

CLR_SCRN.note: Blanks DISPLAYON and clears the frame buffer.

begin_obj.note: A BEGINOBJ wrapper -- DMAWNZ|M_SCRNREL flags and an object id.

BEGINOBJ_TBL.note: Creates an object from a table of its parameters.

DO_REVERSAL_MESS.note: A display process. Its one piece of logic -- RND_AWARD a8,REVERSAL_AWD -- is translated in wm/award.h; the rest is the message object and its voice call.

BONUS_MESS.note: The source's own comment: 'Process which displays high risk - 2x damage & possibly move name'.

meters.note: Builds the two lifebar meter objects and the credit box, then loops. The values it displays are wm/arcade/wm_arcade_life_data.h.

SET_FLASHING.note: Starts the combo-flash process and its sound. The COMBO_FLASH_FLAG guard it wraps is the actor's combo_flash field.

rewire_meter.note: Repoints a meter's objects at a different wrestler in a multi-drone match.

draw_combo_meter.note: Draws the combo bar at a given size.

set_volume.note: send_code_a3 with 55AAh -- a command to the DCS sound board.

read_switches.note: The per-wrestler caching pass. Named for the one wrestler it does rather than the loop, because the port has no process_ptrs array to walk.

init_life_data.note: Named for when it runs. It is the reset that leaves PLT_CLIFE at zero so the bars fill in.

init_wres_life_data.note: The change_wrestler reset, which snaps the displayed bar to full instead.

init_rnd_life_data.note: The round-two reset, which leaves combo and turbo alone.

do_fade.note: The arcade runs it as a process; the port exposes one loop iteration so a caller drives it from whatever scheduler it has.

get_string_len.note: The entry point that presets a4 to message_buffer and falls into get_string_len2. Nothing in the source references the label -- every caller uses get_string_len2 -- so it also reads as dead; both are true.

is_a14_behind.note: The register name in the source's label is not worth carrying into C.

powerup_check.note: AWARD.ASM:2198. Does nothing unless do_show_options is set, then clears both request words and the seven output flags and CREATEs a player_powerup_checker per side. The clearing half is wm_powerup_reset; the processes are the row table.

rst_awards.note: Named for what it clears. Includes the source's sixty-three-byte off-by-one.

accumulate_awards.note: Folds the round arrays into the match arrays, inverting the blocks award on the way.

adjust_perfects.note: The source's name undersells it: it adjusts blocks as well, in a second and differently-shaped pass.

get_num_awards.note: How many rows the end-of-match bar shows, capped at six.

is_it_a_really_quick_win.note: Including the unconditional jruc that makes its SUPER_QUICK and VERY_QUICK branches unreachable.

arm_comeback_award.note: The 80%-health sweep over every live enemy.

change_anim1.note: The guarded primary entry: restart if the animation ended, do nothing if it is already the one playing, else fall into change_anim1a.

change_anim1a.note: The unconditional primary entry, gravity reset included. 503 call sites, the most-referenced routine in the game.

change_anim2a.note: The unconditional secondary entry -- the torso channel, and the one that does NOT reset gravity.

change_anim_anim.note: change_anim1a's body on an arbitrary process rather than a13, and without the immediate animate_wrestler1. The port passes the exec and actor explicitly, so it is the same call.

concat_rom_string.note: The C name reorders the words.

copy_rom_string.note: The C name reorders the words.

get_opp_process.note: The closest-opponent lookup. This port holds one fixed opponent per actor, documented in wm/arcade/wm_arcade_closest.h, so there is nothing to search.

hrt_velocity_table.note: The eight walk-velocity tables have identical BODIES -- the same compass-ordered `.long 0,-#VEL / #DVEL,-#DVEL / ...` in every file -- and differ only in the two per-wrestler equates #VEL and #DVEL. Doink is the one wrestler whose pair differs from the other seven, so the port carries the shape once as a macro and two instantiations (s_velocity_std, s_velocity_doink) behind wm_wrestler_velocity_table(WRESTLERNUM); Bret's predates the shared backend and is wm_bret_velocity_table. Same numbers, one copy of the layout.

hrt_grab_toss_air.note: A secret-move monitor process. BRET.ASM:166's smove table names the routine; the port reaches the same body through a monitor id and wm_arcade_bret_fire_monitor's case for it, with the label kept as the table's own string so the two cannot drift.

hrt_hdhold_ddt.note: Same shape as hrt_grab_toss_air: an smove monitor reached by id.

hrt_hdhold_faceslam.note: Same shape as hrt_grab_toss_air: an smove monitor reached by id.

hrt_roll_uppercut.note: Same shape as hrt_grab_toss_air: an smove monitor reached by id. Its animation is emitted too (hrt_roll_uppercut_anim), and src/core/anim_code.c's rope check redirects into that program's #stand.

lex_hdhold_pile.note: An smove monitor. Lex's dispatcher selects by position in his special_processes list rather than by a named id, so the source label IS the key: wm_arcade_lex_fire_monitor indexes the list and branches on the label's shape.

lex_hdhold_elbow_face.note: An smove monitor, same positional dispatch as lex_hdhold_pile.

std_taunt.note: The taunt monitor every wrestler's smove table carries -- it is defined once in DOINK.ASM and referenced by all eight tables. Present in each wrestler's special_processes list in the port for the same reason it is in each source table.

std_walk_fast.note: The run monitor every wrestler's smove table carries, defined once in DOINK.ASM like std_taunt.

check_collisions.note: The whole attacker/victim sweep, including the source's alternating scan order (round_tick parity) and its exit after the first accepted hit. Named for what it iterates over rather than for the file it came from, which is why the name does not resolve on its own.

wres_collis_off.note: Clears MODE_CHECKHIT. Eleven call sites across the react modules and the lifebar reach it under this name.

set_collision_boxes.note: The source sets BOTH boxes in one routine; the port sets them where each is needed. The hurt box comes from the frame the animation is showing (wm_hurt_box_for_frame / wm_arcade_set_hurt_box in wrestler_backend.c's tick), and the attack box from the attacker just before the collision sweep (wm_arcade_set_attack_box). Splitting them is what lets the hurt box follow real per-frame geometry rather than a single box per wrestler.

hit_push.note: REACT2.ASM:427. The port shares one body between the two reactions that need it, which is why it carries the _common suffix.

CHECK_SCORE.note: The high-score table's placement search, over packed-BCD scores. Prefixed and suffixed to sit beside the rest of the hiscore core.

SPRINKLE_GLINTS.note: The title-screen glint process, translated as a wm_process in src/core/app.c -- the _proc suffix marks it as one, which is what stops the name resolving.

und_spirit_pull.note: One of Undertaker's smove monitors. His dispatcher selects by position in his special_processes list rather than by a named id, so the source label IS the key -- same positional dispatch as lex_hdhold_pile.

und_spirit_push.note: An smove monitor, same positional dispatch as und_spirit_pull.

animate_wrestler.note: ANIM.ASM:68. Its whole body is `animate` on ANIMODE then `animate` on ANIMODE2 -- the two animation channels, in that order, gated on match_time being non-zero. wm_wrestler_backend_tick does exactly that with the primary program and the torso program; wm_anim_exec_tick is the `animate` underneath.

animate_wrestler1.note: ANIM.ASM:92, called from change_anim1a (:4554) right after it writes ANIMODE, ANICNT and the gravity reset: it runs the new animation's first command immediately rather than waiting a tick. The port's exec_start ends with the same advance() call, so starting an animation already shows its first frame. Its other call site is commented out in the source (:76).

animate_wrestler2.note: ANIM.ASM:103, the secondary channel's half of animate_wrestler1 and inlined the same way -- change_anim2a's own advance(). Its other call site is commented out at :77.

attacker_flip_test.note: The defender's attach offset uses its own aniX, or (xsize - aniX) when the puppet table's flip disagrees with which way the attacker is facing. src/core/anim_program.c's run_superslave2 spells that out at its one use site, reading real per-frame geometry rather than a guessed width.

set_xyz.note: COLLIS.ASM:669. Builds the ATTACK box in world space from OBJ_ATT{X,Y,Z}OFF and OBJ_ATT{WIDTH,HEIGHT,DEPTH}, including the FLIPH branch that mirrors the X extent for a wrestler facing left. wm_arcade_set_attack_box is that routine line for line; it is named for what it produces rather than for the three axes it writes.

check_collis.note: COLLIS.ASM:486. The whole rejection chain -- MODE_NOCOLLIS, IMMOBILIZE_TIME, the six box comparisons, SMART_ATTACK's target, combo mode's WHOIHIT, a dead victim with live teammates, AMODE_PUPPET on a corpse, ZOMBIE, PINNED without DID_PIN, mismatched INRING, AMODE_PUSH against a man in the air, the victim's own PUSH bit -- then MODE_WAITHITOPP's clear, HITBLOCKER, PLYR_HIT_SIDE from the X and Z comparison, MODE_STATUS and wrestler_hit. The port returns a wm_arcade_hit_result_t where the source reports through the attacker's MODE_STATUS bit.

hit_flykick.note: REACT1.ASM:1421. Halves the attacker's X velocity, clamps the magnitude to 4.0 once it reaches 2.0, flips its sign away from his travel and sets Y to 4.0; then Lex's two kicks take CALL_MID_HIT where everyone else takes CALL_DROP_KICK, and the victim falls back with a 2.0 push. Named in a comment in wm_arcade_react8_core.c, which is why the automatic pass reads it as cited rather than translated.

hit_grabhold.note: REACT2.ASM:363. Every line of its body is commented out, including the #heldoh table, so it assembles to nothing and falls straight through into hit_grabfling's rets at :396. WM_RXN_GRABHOLD is therefore a break in the dispatch, which is what the source does.

hit_grabfling.note: REACT2.ASM:396, a bare rets under the source's own comment 'Blank amode here....'. WM_RXN_GRABFLING is a break in the dispatch.

hit_buttstomp.note: REACT4.ASM:107 -- a second label on REACT4.ASM:106 hit_stomp's body, with no instruction between them. AMODE_STOMP and AMODE_BUTTSTOMP run the same code and the port dispatches both to the same function.

hit_headhold.note: REACT4.ASM:523, a bare rets. WM_RXN_HEADHOLD is a break in the dispatch.

hit_headdslash.note: REACT9.ASM:145. The down-slash and the up-slash (REACT9.ASM:195) differ in exactly two things: the Y velocity they give the victim -- 2C000h against 40000h -- and the five-pixel shove toward the attacker that only the down-slash adds. Both share the dead-victim fall_back tail, so the port writes one function with a flag.

hit_headuslash.note: REACT9.ASM:195. The up-slash half of hit_headslash_common: Y velocity 40000h, X zeroed, and no shove toward the attacker.

set_images.note: ANIM.ASM:4612, and #set_image at :4632 which it runs over every wrestler. The part that is game logic is translated in wm/match_display.h: OBJ_PRIORITY (z_fixed | 01000h, less 01e5h below the mat when outside the ring), the shadow's fixed 013c8h/0106ah, OYVAL as z_int * Y_SCALE_MULTIPLIER, the GROUND_Y shadow offset against the body's OBJ_YPOSINT, and MODE_INVISIBLE and MODE_NOSHADOW. The part that is not is the object plumbing -- walking OBJ_BASE's MAX_PIECES DMA slots, writing OSAG/OSIZE/OCTRL/OCONST, the multi-piece IPCOUNT loop and the palette handoff to pal_getf -- which is hardware this port replaces rather than translates.

drone_seek.note: DRONE.ASM:3027 -- `movi 70,a2` and fall straight into drone_seek2. Two labels, one body; the 70 is the only thing drone_seek contributes.

drone_seek2.note: DRONE.ASM:3031 -- reads the opponent's XZ and falls into drone_seekxz. The port folds all three labels into seekxz_joy plus the two callers that supply a range; seek_plain70 is this one, and seek_drn_seek adds drn_seek's own mode gate and 1/64 stop roll on top.

drone_seekxz.note: DRONE.ASM:3046 -- the joystick word that walks a drone toward an XZ point, one axis at a time: `subk 4 / addk 8` for the X pair and `subk 1 / addk 2` for the Z pair, each suppressed while that axis is already within range. Returns zero once both are, which is the source's own `move a0,a0 / rets` pass-CC arrival test.

drone_seekdirdist.note: DRONE.ASM:2898 -- circling. #drn_getxz's six 16-entry sine bands are in s_sine_band, including the quarter-cycle phase shift that reads X out of the same table as Z, and the eight-step search outward from the wanted direction when the exact one lands outside the ring. The +-2/3 reroll on arrival happens only when DRN_MODE was -1, as the source's `addk 1,a0 / jrge #x` requires.

rope_update.note: ROPES.ASM:439 -- the per-tick rope animation stepper: PD_SQCNT down to the next frame, PD_SQPTR for the next time increment with its jrp/jrn split into next-frame and sequence-goto, PD_SCCNT's repeat and PD_SCPTR's advance to the next script entry. wmania_rope_runtime.c carries all of it, including the end-of-script clear of the long at PD_SQCNT that takes the priority with it.

set_rope_z.note: ROPES.ASM:593 -- the bottom half of a rope object takes 015a9h for RZ_HIGH and otherwise copies the top half's OZPOS. The port keeps the constant as WM_ROPE_HIGH_SECOND_HALF_Z and the choice as this function; writing it into an object is the renderer's.

fastanic.note: ROPES.ASM:558 -- point a DMA object at a new image: ODOFF, OIMG, OSIZE, OSAG and the five z-compare bits of OCTRL, plus a CALLERR if the image pointer is below ROM. Every line writes the object hardware and there is nothing else in it.

update_meter.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:1257 -- redraw one meter: OFSET set to LIFE_MAX minus the displayed life (the pixels to hide), then the M_NODISP toggle for a wrestler who is OUTSIDE_ALONE and the WHICH_SCREEN check behind it. The value it draws, PLT_CLIFE, is real and is wm_life_inc_life's; the drawing is not.

do_win_streaks.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:2164 -- build the two-digit win-streak display for each player: clamp to 99, BINBCD, index #f_t for each nibble's digit image and BEGINOBJ it at a fixed screen position, plus the `lwin` label object. It reads p1winstreak/p2winstreak and writes only objects.

get_punch_dtime.note: WRESTLE.ASM:3994. Three instructions -- scale PLYRNUM, index punch_dtime1, read the word. The port keeps the nine hold counters on the actor rather than in nine parallel arrays, so the index is the actor and the array is a wm_arcade_dtime_t.

get_powerp_dtime.note: WRESTLE.ASM:3985, the same three instructions against powerp_dtime1. WM_DTIME_POWERP.

update_timer.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:4370. Reads the two match_time digits, indexes digit_tbl for each one's image and hands it to change_image against the two PDATA object pointers. The clock value itself is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_round.h's; this is the two digits on screen.

ZERO_BITS.note: UTIL.ASM:103. Clears BAKBITS -- 10000/16 words of the machine's own bitmap RAM -- with a word-store loop. There is no BAKBITS on an N64.

WIPEOUT.note: UTIL.ASM:122. dirq_wait, display_init, then pal_init inside a dint, and fall through to WIPEOUT2: reset the machine between screens. Every line is the cabinet's display processor or its palette RAM.

WIPEOUT2.note: UTIL.ASM:136. The rest of the reset: zero a dozen globals, KILALL every process, ZERO_BITS the bitmap, dpageflip_off, then write SYSCTRL from SYSCOPY (with the WWFUNIT variant that leaves the 7-segment LED alone). Process and hardware state this port does not have.

SPECIAL_WIPEOUT.note: UTIL.ASM:113. WIPEOUT2 then a jump to SPECIAL_DISPLAY_INIT -- the same reset with a different display mode after it.

adjust_bar_height.note: MENU.ASM:840. Grows or shrinks the operator volume bar one line at a time toward a target, drawing each line through vol_bar_line. The bar is pixels in the frame buffer.

vol_bar_line.note: MENU.ASM:866. Plots one line of the volume bar with cvxyl and a byte-store loop, skipping pixels that already hold the text colour -- the source's own "won't overwrite green pixels (text)", which the code actually tests against ROBO_BLUE after a commented-out ROBO_GREEN. Direct frame-buffer writes.

addbae.note: PAL.ASM:1032. Three instructions and a fallthrough into pal_addb's body at pb1c, with the autoerase colour (IRQSKYE/irqskyeo) as the palette and a count of one. The arithmetic -- including the unsigned clamp that turns a negative brightness into full brightness rather than zero -- is wm_pal_addb's, already translated with that quirk intact.

addbrt_ae.note: PAL.ASM:1009. A CREATE0'd process that ramps the autoerase brightness from 0 (up fade) or 31 (down fade) by A10 every three ticks until it passes 31, calling addbae each step, then DIEs. The step is addbae's; the loop is a process and a SLEEPK.

bcd2hex.note: DIAG.ASM:417. Eight-digit BCD to binary, by repeated mask-multiply-accumulate. Portable arithmetic, but it exists only for the PIC security chip: its two callers (DIAG.ASM:600 and :612) both convert a serial number read out of PIC_COMMAND, and that chip is the cabinet's.

bin2bcd.note: DIAG.ASM:381 _pic_bin2bcd. The inverse, by repeated divide-by-a-descending-power-of-ten. Same three callers, same reason: it formats the PIC serial number for the diagnostics screen.

no_block_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:1967 -- three blocks, and it DIEs outright in a royal rumble. It shares its opening presses with buddy_mode (five blocks), which player_powerup_checker starts on the same side at the same time, so a player going for buddy mode turns blocking off on the way past.

move_names_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:1992 -- four punches, setting MOVE_NAMES_ON. It is one of the two bits outside BOTH_P_MASK, so one player asking is enough.

drone_meters_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2016 -- and it has no sequence at all: all three of its PUPWAITSWITCH lines are commented out, so once its two gates pass (PSTATUS != 3, 'only in one-player games'; NUM_OPPS == 1, 'only in one-on-one games') it sets D_METERS_ON immediately. The table carries it with a zero-length sequence and wm_powerup_attempt_done reports it complete from the start.

hyper_match_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2052 -- left, punch, punch, block. The `ori HYPER_MATCH_ON` carries the source's own comment '; Disabled for now', but nothing about the routine is disabled: it is created, it listens, and it sets the bit.

combos_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2075 -- right, punch, power punch, setting COMBOS_ON. This is where wm_arcade_mode_dead.h's instant_combos_on comes from.

ring_out_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2097 -- down, punch, kick, block.

no_ring_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2120 -- up, right, down, left. A complete code with nothing listening for it: player_powerup_checker's CREATE for it is commented out, 'Disable until we get blimp module'. The table records the sequence and marks it not spawned.

buddy_mode_powerup_check.note: The whole powerup-code subsystem is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_powerup.h: the eight sequences as data, PUPWAITSWITCH as wm_powerup_attempt_tick, and get_powerups' BOTH_P_MASK reconciliation. AWARD.ASM:2146 -- five blocks, blocked in a royal rumble, and the only one with a second gate: it clears buddy_mode_checked at the top of its loop and refuses to grant if something has set it again by the time the fifth block lands.

player_powerup_checker.note: AWARD.ASM:2182. Seven CREATEs and a DIE -- one checker process per code, per side. The port runs the same eight-row table without processes, and the row's `spawned` flag carries the one CREATE that is commented out.

accumulate_player_awards.note: AWARD.ASM:257. Folds one player's NUM_RND_AWARDS round bytes into his match bytes, after inverting BLOCKS_AWD -- having taken no blocks is what earns the icons, so a nonzero count becomes zero and a zero becomes BLOCK_ICONS. Skipped entirely in a royal rumble or when that player's process slot is empty.

rst_winstreak_awards.note: AWARD.ASM:314. `movi NUM_AWARDS-1,a0` and a dsjs loop, so it clears 31 of the 32 words and leaves the last alone -- almost certainly a slip, since the sibling rst_awards uses the full count, and unobservable because the highest award index in use is FIVE_WINS at 29. The port reproduces it rather than quietly correcting it.

give_award_if_opponent_is_human.note: AWARD.ASM:1032. DEFEAT_HUMAN, granted on each side by testing the OTHER side's PSTATUS bit -- bit 0 is 'player 1 is in', bit 1 is 'player 2 is in'.

check_for_award_for_big_comeback.note: AWARD.ASM:1096. Grants COMEBACK_AWD if this side's pcomeback flag is armed; arm_comeback_award is what arms it, and only when every live enemy is still at 80% health or better.

check_for_award_for_winstreak.note: AWARD.ASM:1152. Grants FIVE_WINS_AWD if this side's pwsarm flag is set, and clears the flag so it is granted once.

arm_winstreak_award.note: AWARD.ASM:1124. Arms pwsarm when the streak is a nonzero multiple of five (`movk 5,a0 / modu a0,a1 / jrnz #awa_disarm`), and explicitly DISarms it otherwise -- so reaching six wins takes the pending award away again rather than leaving it standing.

FIND_LOW_TABLE_LEVEL.note: HSTD.ASM:3358. Walk the table from entry 1 down and report the first slot this score beats, or zero. It and FIND_HIGH_TABLE_LEVEL at :3322 are the same routine with one instruction different -- `JRLO` here against `JRGE` there -- which is why a lower pin time and a higher win streak both sort to the front. wm_hs_find_level carries both as the table's own WM_HS_HIGHER_IS_BETTER flag.

pin_speed_check.note: HSTD.ASM:1865. Three refusals before the table is even consulted: a drone (index >= 2) never enters, a match that took three rounds never counts (`cmpi 3,a14 / jreq #retp`), and a non-positive MATCH_TIMERS entry is dropped. Only then does FIND_LOW_TABLE_LEVEL get a look.

winstreak_check.note: HSTD.ASM:1889. Unlike pin_speed_check it has no gate at all -- it reads p1oldwinstreak and goes straight to FIND_HIGH_TABLE_LEVEL, which is the only thing that can turn it away.

DO_TAG_GAME.note: HSTD.ASM:1846. Clears this player's entered_inits, then enters the tag table through FIND_LOW_TABLE_LEVEL with do_entry_time as the entry routine.

are_inits_dirty.note: HSTD.ASM:2631. The profanity filter: pack each letter into five bits (`subi 40h / andi 1fh`), skipping the three non-alpha grid cells 19h, 20h and 21h, and compare the running value against #dw_table after every letter -- so a banned word is caught as a prefix, not only as the whole entry.

INIT_HSTRING.note: HSTD.ASM:3602. Four KILL_AUD calls -- winstreak, pinspeed, beaten and tag -- and a rets. It is reached from the VAL_TAB path when a table had to be reinitialised, and clearing those audit markers is the whole of it. Notably it does NOT clear AUD_INTER.

INIT_TB.note: HSTD.ASM:3623. Copy a table factory entries out of ROM into CMOS a byte at a time, then walk back down every entry INCLUDING the zero one writing its checksum. wm_hs_init_table does the same from the WmHsFactoryEntry rows, and wm_hs_rechecksum is the per-entry half.

new_cursor_pos.note: HSTD.ASM:2692. Places the initials-entry cursor and highlight objects on the letter grid and picks the character image under them. Worth one note even though it is display: the grid is FIVE columns wide, `movk 5,a0 / modu` for the X and `movk 5,a2 / divu` for the Y, and the source's own comments above both lines say `mod 6` and `/ 6`.

print_hscores.note: HSTD.ASM:636. Draws a whole high-score table: the heading, then a row per entry through draw_*_table_entry. The tables and their ordering are wmania_hiscore_core's; this is the page.

print_init_string.note: HSTD.ASM. Redraws the three initials being entered as objects under the cursor.

MOVE_ALL_OBJS_UP.note: HSTD.ASM:512. Gives every object on the high-score page an upward Y velocity so the table scrolls off. Object motion, nothing else.

STOP_ALL_OBJS.note: HSTD.ASM:501. Zeroes every object's velocity -- the other half of the scroll.

DELETE_ANY_OFF_TOP.note: HSTD.ASM:531. Deletes objects once the scroll has carried them above the screen.

JUDDER_SHADOW.note: HSTD.ASM. A FLASH_PID process that shakes the drop shadow behind the high-score heading. A CREATE, a loop and an object offset.

init_special_objlist.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1278. Three stores: the heads of plyr1_objlist, plyr2_objlist and neutral_objlist. Which of the three a projectile joins is decided by SP_PLYR_SIDE, where -1 is neutral.

delete_special_objlist.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1312. Unlink a projectile from whichever of the three lists its SP_PLYR_SIDE puts it in, walking from the head. The insert half is insert_special_objlist at :1292, which the port keeps as wm_arcade_special_insert.

sp_change_anim.note: SPECIAL.ASM:2197. Point a projectile at a new animation script and run its immediate non-image opcodes straight away through sp_animate -- which is why the port's change_anim executes them rather than waiting a tick.

sp_animate.note: SPECIAL.ASM:2208. The projectile animation stepper sp_change_anim falls into; the port folds both into one function, since the only caller of the stepper is the change.

yok_salt_spray.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1679. Yokozuna's salt: the constructor's exact SP_ field state, which wm_arcade_spawn_yoko_salt carries value for value, plus the salt-specific grow-then-live transitions (wm_arcade_special_salt_become_live and _salt_disable_collision).

create_dizzy_proc.note: SPECIAL.ASM:87. The stars over a dizzy wrestler. Its gate (STARS_FLAG, one set at a time) and its per-wrestler offset are translated in the animation VM; the star itself is a DEBRIS_PID object, so the VM reaches it through wm_anim_env's create_dizzy seam.

begin_ani.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1200. Reads a projectile process's XVAL/YVAL/ZVAL/FLAGS/XVEL/YVEL and the first entry of its animation script, then BEGINOBJP. Object creation start to finish.

special_ani.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1224. One tick of a projectile's object animation: count down, fetch the next (ticks, image) pair, write OIMG/OSIZE/OSAG/ODXOFF/ODYOFF and the five z-compare bits, and DELOBJA8 plus DIE on a zero tick count. The two `add a10,a1` / `add a11,a1` offset lines are commented out, so the anim offsets are used raw.

change_image_local.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1259. special_ani's image write on its own: OIMG, OSIZE, OSAG, the two display offsets and the z-compare byte.

impact_proc.note: SPECIAL.ASM:843. A DEBRIS_PID process that plays one impact burst and dies. The decision to create it, and how many pieces, is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_debris.h's; the pieces are objects.

impact_proc2.note: SPECIAL.ASM:830. The same, with the second burst's image set.

dizzy_proc.note: SPECIAL.ASM:158. The star process create_dizzy_proc spawns: orbit the wrestler's head until STARS_FLAG clears, then die.

create_impact3.note: SPECIAL.ASM:397. Two refusals then a CREATE: `@no_debris` and `@reduce_bog` both abort it outright, which is the same pair wm/arcade/wm_arcade_debris.h already gates on. What is left is the DEBRIS_PID creation at a fixed 58h offset.

react_blood.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1846. Sets a projectile's gravity to GRAVITY*2 and its DMA flags, then BEGINOBJs a PINSHAD1 at z 150. The second BEGINOBJ below it, for the shadow at z 149, is commented out -- so SP_SHADOW_OBJ is explicitly cleared at the top and never filled.

react_bloodnguts_gen.note: SPECIAL.ASM:1805. The generator that spawns react_blood processes. Its gates are the shared debris ones; the spray is objects.

init_joystat.note: WRESTLE.ASM:4533. Zero round_tickcount and clear the whole wrest_joystat ring buffer. The port holds the tick count at the call site rather than in the buffer, so the clear is wm_arcade_joystat_init and the counter is the caller's.

reset_smoves.note: WRESTLE.ASM:6140. Walk the ACTIVE process list and, for every SMOVE_PID, point PWAKE at that watchdog's SM_RESET_ADDRESS and set PTIME to 1 -- restart every special-move detector at once. This port detects secret moves by matching wm_arcade_joystat's ring buffer rather than by running a process per move, so there is nothing to restart: the equivalent is the buffer itself, which init_joystat clears.

switch_unstack.note: WRESTLE.ASM:551. Drain the coin/service switch queue: pop an entry, index switch_t by switch number times three, and GETPRC a process to handle it. The queue is filled by the switch interrupt and the table is the cabinet's wiring.

crowd_anim.note: CROWD.ASM:80. Thirty crowd blocks, each running its own script through animate_back, plus the BAKLST sweep that pushes the current frame into the background objects. The part this port has is the cheer seam the game pokes it with (wm_anim_env's crowd_cheer/crowd_sound and DO_CROWD_CHEER's gates); the part it does not is the background animation itself -- a six-command bytecode VM and ninety scripts (thirty spectators times norm/cheer1/cheer2, CROWD.ASM:295). Spectator artwork, not fight logic.

animate_back.note: CROWD.ASM:126. One tick of one crowd block: count down TIME, and on zero read the next script word -- a negative word is one of six commands (goto, rndwait, end, code, random-repeat, should-we-repeat) and a positive one is a tick count followed by a frame pointer. Its exit carries a deliberate curiosity the source flags itself: it writes zero into A14 as `MOVK 1,A14 / DEC A14` under the comment "You think a simple CLR would do the job here? Try it. I dare you." -- because the assembler's CLR expands to MOVK 0, which on a TMS34010 does NOT set the status flags, and the caller branches on Z.

ck_ignore_a8.note: WRESTLE.ASM:6044. Both callers -- BRET.ASM:596 and DOINK.ASM:1399 -- gate the FLYING KICK on it: you cannot launch one while backing away. mv_tbl (:6035) is indexed by NEW_FACING_DIR and yields a BIT NUMBER tested in MOVE_DIR, so facing 5 or 6 tests MOVE_RIGHT and facing 9 or 10 tests MOVE_LEFT -- always 'away from where he is looking'. A facing outside those four would read a zero from the table, which is bit number zero, MOVE_UP; the source's own comment says the facing is '(9,10,6,5 only)', so the port answers allow rather than reproducing a lookup the comment rules out.

get_box_overlap.note: WRESTLE.ASM:5704. Given a box made of two boundary lines, the shortest push that gets a wrestler out of it: four edge distances, smallest wins, ties to the horizontal because every comparison is a strict jrgt. Note the Z bounds come from whichever seed a6 held LAST, which is the left line. It reports (0,0) both for 'not in the box' and for a Z outside the lines' range, so a caller cannot tell those apart. No live caller: all four call sites (:5545, :5584, :5633, :5682) are commented out.

drn_combo.note: DRONE.ASM:2092. Its first act is `#wres_t[WRESTLERNUM]` and a jump, so it is really eight scripts. All eight are in the port's table and differ only in which two buttons their 50% flip chooses between -- everyone opens with the same two reversals and everyone ends in #cstrt. Slot 7, the cut wrestler, is given Doink's by the table itself. Nothing selects drn_combo in this port: CHECK_COMBO_GO can never report a lit combo meter while nothing fills one (wm/arcade/wm_arcade_mode_dead.h).

change_walk_anim.note: WRESTLE.ASM:4946. Reselect the leg cycle for the direction a wrestler is walking, and the torso with it. Reached only from the eight real-movement arms of execute_walk's dispatch, i.e. under MOVE_DIR != 0. The port gates the torso half on its single anim_mode where the source uses ANIMODE2; nothing here writes an ANIMODE2, so that is the primary channel's mode -- the same approximation Bret's backend has always made.

set_rotate_anim.note: WRESTLE.ASM:5062. change_walk_anim's counterpart on the idle path: no movement, so the turn animation is chosen from the facing alone. Both halves live in wm_wrestler_backend_execute_walk, which is the dispatch that picks between them.

update_joystat.note: WRESTLE.ASM:4569. Push this tick's input into the shared history ring: LEFT/RIGHT absolute at bits 10-11, the facing-relative direction at bits 0-3 (run through xflip_table at :4650 when facing left, which swaps only LEFT and RIGHT), and one entry per newly pressed button tagged at bits 4-8. Inserted only on a stick edge with a nonzero value, or on a button press.

increment_wincount.note: WRESTLE.ASM. Credit a round to a side. The port keeps the score in wm_arcade_match_score and awards through the round-announce path the animation VM already reaches.

init_reduce_bog.note: WRESTLE.ASM:4552. Count active wrestler processes, subtract two, and store the remainder in reduce_bog -- so a straight one-on-one leaves it at zero and every extra wrestler raises it. It is a load-shedding level, not a flag, and the debris and move-name code both read it.

set_up_line_tables.note: WRESTLE.ASM:5834. Precompute a per-Z lookup for each of the eight boundary lines at startup, stepping a 16.16 accumulator by (width<<16)/(depth+1) and reading index i AFTER i+1 steps -- so entry 0 is not top_x but one step past it. The port computes the closed form directly instead of building the tables, which is the same arithmetic including that off-by-one, and needs no boot phase this port has not got.

start_match.note: WRESTLE.ASM:1900. The match's own setup and main loop. Translated: the PSTATUS==0 attract path in full -- the RNDRNG0(7)-skip-7 wrestler draw, init_life_data, the PLYRNUM/PSIDE actor creation, and the SLEEP 3*60 plus wait_on_butn 10*TSEC timing. Not translated: the process creation for every other game mode, the scroller and background startup, and the CREATE-based subsystems (smoves, crowd, lifebar) this port has no processes for.

change_wrestler.note: WRESTLE2.ASM. Swap a dead wrestler for a fresh one mid-match. The life-table half is wm_life_init_wrestler, and its distinguishing detail is translated: CLIFE snaps to FULL rather than starting at zero, because the bar must not animate up for a replacement.

flash_red.note: WRESTLE2.ASM. Flashes the life bar red on a hit. Pure lifebar rendering -- wm/arcade/wm_arcade_lifebar.h already records it as the one piece of adjust_health's tail that is drawing rather than damage.

match_timer.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:4155. The round clock and the KO detection around it. Translated: the countdown, the difficulty-based decrement rate and the round-decided transition, in wm/arcade/wm_arcade_round.h. Not translated: the KO-detection loop's process bookkeeping and the digit drawing, which is update_timer.

init_smoves.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:4055. Called once per MATCH, not per round: it CREATEs one watchdog process per entry in this wrestler's #special_moves list -- the moves the ordinary secret-move matcher cannot handle, the source says, because they involve charging a stick, exact timing, or proximity. This port has no processes; it matches patterns against wm_arcade_joystat's ring instead, and the per-wrestler move lists are wm/wrestler_anim_tables.h's.

kill_smove_procs.note: WRESTLE2.ASM. The other end of init_smoves: kill every SMOVE_PID. Nothing to kill here.

ditch_getup_meter_a9.note: WRESTLE2.ASM. Drop a wrestler's getup meter, reached from keep_onscreen when a run is stopped and from the react layer. The port carries it as a callback on wm_arcade_react_callbacks_t because the meter is a display object the core does not own.

obj_yzsort.note: DISPLAY.ASM:1248. Bubble-sort the object list into ascending OZPOS, then ascending OYPOS within an equal OZPOS. Those are the values #set_image writes, and both are derived from Z, so the second key cannot separate two wrestlers at the same depth -- the port's draw list reproduces the comparison rather than the bubble sort.

wait_on_butn.note: ATTRACT.ASM. Sleep until a button is pressed or a timeout expires, whichever first. The attract sequence's real timings -- SLEEP TSEC/2 then wait_on_butn 8*TSEC, and show_gameplay's SLEEP 3*60 then wait_on_butn 10*TSEC -- are translated in wm/app.h as tick counts, because this port advances the app a tick at a time rather than sleeping a process.

display_blank.note: UTIL.ASM. Turns the display processor off. There is no display processor.

RemapIO.note: MAIN.ASM. Moves the I/O window in the address map. Its one call site in WRESTLE.ASM's main loop is commented out, under the author's own question: "isn't there a less obvious place that we can remap the IO ???"

fallbacks_t.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:1849. Nine REFLONGs, and they are the SAME nine as REACT1.ASM:1801 fall_back_tbl -- hrt_fall_back_anim down to lex_fall_back_anim with slot 7 empty. Already extracted under that name into src/generated/roster_anim_tables.c. tools/wlrostertbl.py does not see this copy because three labels stand in a row above the rows (`SUBR fallbacks_t`, then `#fallbacks_t`, then `#fall_back`) and its reader stops at the second. Teaching it to walk an alias chain was tried and reverted: it misattributed rows across the tree and cost fourteen tables that were being read correctly, for two whose contents are already here.

convulse_t.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:1863. The same story: nine REFLONGs identical to REACT1.ASM:1856 hitonground_tbl, behind the alias chain `SUBR convulse_t` / `#hitonground`.

raise_dead.note: FINISEQ.ASM:1535. `SLEEP TSEC/2` -- "Give him a bit before standing up" -- then put @dead_wrestler into raise_dead_anim and DIE. A CREATE'd delay around one change_anim1a.

get_mpart_offsets.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:1509. Walks a multi-part image's IPCOUNT pieces and returns the largest IANIOFFX/IANIOFFY among them -- the bounding anchor for a sprite drawn as several DMA objects. The port has one frame geometry per frame (wm/frame_geometry.h) rather than a piece list, so there is nothing to walk.

get_mpart_xsize.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:1566. The same walk for the total width.

slide_offscr.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:1045. A process that gives an object a velocity and waits for it to leave the screen. Object motion.

postgame_audits.note: WRESTLE2.ASM:4662. Writes the match's counters into CMOS audit storage. There is no CMOS.

audit_wrestler.note: WRESTLE2.ASM. Bumps the per-wrestler CMOS audit counter.

print_string_with_zb.note: STRING.ASM:585. print_string with a Z-buffer value supplied, so the text sorts against the scene rather than sitting on top. The layout half is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_string.h's; the Z is the object's.

UNDBLU_P.note: WRESPAL.ASM:136. One of the Undertaker's palettes. The palette corpus is extracted wholesale by tools/wlpal.py into src/generated/palettes.c, so this is a row in generated data rather than a routine anything calls.

rnd.note: DISPLAY.ASM:1212. The shared RAND mix -- rotate by RAND's own low five bits, rotate in HCOUNT, add SP, store back -- then mask the result with A0. It is the same body as UTIL.ASM's, and wm/arcade/wmania_rng.h carries it together with the warning that `add sp,a1` is the only value-changing step, so a caller that leaves both entropy inputs at zero gets a degenerate sequence rather than a weak one.

is_there_one_already.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:3424. MOVE_NAME_ANNC's "first time only" rule: index MESSAGE_FLAGS by the INVERTED low bit of the side (`NOT A1 / SLL 31 / SRL 31-4`) and read the flag. The port folds the test and its companion SET_MESS_FLAGS into wm_move_name_should_draw, which is also where reduce_bog's suppression lives.

adjust_taker_facing.note: FINISEQ.ASM:1032. The exact mirror of adjust_facing at :1018 -- one ORs LEFT|DOWN in and masks RIGHT|UP off and sets FLIPH, the other does the reverse -- so the port carries one body with the direction as its registry parameter. src/core/anim_code.c registers it as `{ "adjust_taker_facing", "FINISEQ.ASM", adjust_facing, 1, 0 }`; the name reaches the VM, it just is not a separate C function.

stand_wrestler.note: FINISEQ.ASM:1488. A FACETBL index into :1471 stand_table and a change_anim1a on a13 -- nothing else. dizzy_wrestler at :1505 is the same two instructions against :1493 dizzy_table, so the port carries one body and picks the table with the registry parameter. The nine rows of each table are read out of the source by tools/wlpuppet.py's CODE_TABLES into src/generated/anim_aux_tables.c, not transcribed.

dizzy_wrestler.note: FINISEQ.ASM:1505. See stand_wrestler: the same body with the other FACETBL, registered as `{ "dizzy_wrestler", "FINISEQ.ASM", coffin_change_by_roster, 1, 0 }`.

und_coffin_up.note: FINISEQ.ASM:580. The mat process: BEGINOBJ the mat at [HOLE_XPOS,HOLE_YPOS], step #mat_anim with SLEEPK 3 + obj_aniq, split it into MATCOF05B/05A, fire 25 ltl_exp, CREATE0 do_up_coffin, wait on @close_the_floor, run #mat_anim2 BACKWARDS, then raise the tombstone. Everything it does is object choreography this port has no renderer for. What it DECIDES is translated: its first two instructions (clear both globals) are wm_coffin_reset, the state values it writes (@close_the_floor 1/2/3 and @finish_completed 3) are documented on wm_coffin_state_t, and the frame lists it walks -- forwards and backwards -- are wm_coffin_mat_frames with wm_coffin_close_frame. Worth recording that :645's `calla DELOBJA8` deletes the FRONT piece despite its comment saying back: a8 was overwritten by the second BEGINOBJ at :623 and the back piece is the one saved in a11.

do_up_coffin.note: FINISEQ.ASM:702. The coffin process, created by und_coffin_up. Same split: the BEGINOBJ/obj_aniq/DELOBJA8 choreography is display, and the arithmetic inside it is translated -- the rise and fall ramps (wm_coffin_rise_step / wm_coffin_fall_step, OSIZEY against OYPOS in steps of COFFIN_VEL), the door's frame walk forwards and backwards (wm_coffin_door_frames, wm_coffin_close_frame), the door-slam shake (wm_coffin_shake_offset, whose Y jitter is -2..0 rather than symmetric), and the @close_the_door 1/3 and @close_the_floor 1 transitions on wm_coffin_state_t.

hover_coffin.note: FINISEQ.ASM:879. A two-object bob that runs until do_up_coffin kills it. The process shell (SLEEPK 7, the OYPOS writes, the CREATE0 ltl_exp burst) is display; one iteration of its state machine is wm_coffin_hover_step, including the asymmetry that makes it interesting -- the turnaround is `movk 1,a8 / not a8`, a ones complement, so the up delta is -2 and not the -1 the comment beside it claims.

ltl_exp.note: FINISEQ.ASM:474. One puff of smoke, created 25 at a time and again on every hover turnaround. The BEGINOBJ, the SNDSND and the three-tick frame walk are display; its six RNDRNG0 draws -- delay, X, Y, Z, velocity and which of the two smoke lists -- are wm_coffin_ltl_exp_params, in the source's own order, because they come off one shared stream.

tstone_test.note: FINISEQ.ASM:573. A `.long` list of image headers, TMBSTN02..TMBSTN08 and a terminator, and the one the shipped game actually raises: und_coffin_up:668 has `movi #tstone_anim,a9` commented out with `movi #tstone_test,a9` beneath it. Kept as the source's own image names, since this port has no image headers yet.

tstone_anim.note: FINISEQ.ASM:571. One `.long`, TMBSTN01, immediately followed by #tstone_test. Starting the tombstone here would show that frame first; the line that did is commented out at :668, so the frame is recorded as WM_COFFIN_TSTONE_UNUSED_FIRST rather than put in the live list.

mat_anim.note: FINISEQ.ASM:552. MATCOF01..MATCOF04, the mat opening. The closing loop at :652 walks this same list backwards, so there is no separate close list.

mat_anim2.note: FINISEQ.ASM:557. Not an animation: a bare `.long 0` sitting immediately after #mat_anim, used as the END pointer that #fc_loop walks backwards from with `move *-a9`. The port expresses that as wm_coffin_close_frame over wm_coffin_mat_frames rather than as a second list.

cof_anim1.note: FINISEQ.ASM:560. COFFIN02..COFFIN05, the coffin door opening. #close_loop at :786 walks it backwards to shut the door, ending on COFFIN02 -- the frame that also drops the front half and moves the Z in front of the wrestler.

cof_anim2.note: FINISEQ.ASM:565. The same shape as #mat_anim2: a bare `.long 0` after #cof_anim1, serving as the backwards walk's start.

exp1_anim.note: FINISEQ.ASM:443. SMOKE01..SMOKE10, one of the two puffs ltl_exp draws between.

ltl_puff.note: FINISEQ.ASM:470. Two `.long`s, pointers to #exp1_anim and #exp2_anim. ltl_exp indexes it with RNDRNG0(1) scaled by 32 -- the stride of a `.long` -- so the draw is just the index, and the port keeps the two lists rather than a table of pointers to them.
